clue.text: Rushes to relative with vermouth

parts.note: a stepson is a relative by marriage
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in 'gin and it'

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to a family member with a bottle of vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth comes from the old bar order 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on it is an idiom for hurrying, as a driver presses the accelerator.

clue.text: Break down one of the overheads at Wimbledon

definitions.text: one of the overheads at Wimbledon

explanation.surface: A tennis player collapses during an overhead shot at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; an overhead there is a high shot hit down hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To break something down by force is to shatter it, and a hard downward overhead stroke in tennis bears the same name.

clue.text: First person to upset female supporter confident of having opening for gun

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for the first person is read backwards

parts.note: the first person singular pronoun as object is me
a bra supports a woman's bust
sure means confident

explanation.surface: A man knocks over a woman's underwear while sure of a gap to shoot through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the pronoun for the first person; 'of having' only joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasure is a splayed slot in a wall or parapet through which a cannon is fired.

clue.text: Perpendicular? Honest it is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a line is vertical and is assured that it truly is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bolt upright stands vertical, and 'it's the truth, honestly' is the British slang assurance of the same phrase.

clue.text: Flowers keeping informer in high spirits

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
gay in its old sense means merry, in high spirits

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers keeps a police informant cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' suggests a container, but the two pieces simply sit side by side; 'keeping' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bouquet of blooms, carried originally for its scent.

clue.text: Change of direction in work of capstan operator

explanation.surface: A sailor at the capstan alters course.
explanation.walkthrough: A capstan lathe is a machine tool; its operator shapes metal on it, which is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bend or veer in a road is one sense; shaping material on a lathe is the other.

clue.text: Upset when given the chop

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed at being axed from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being distressed is one sense; something sliced into pieces by chopping is the other.

clue.text: Third class ought to press head with both sexes together

parts.note: C is the third grade or class after A and B
ought is an old form of nought, zero, so O
the head of a newspaper is its editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A third-class pupil is told to lean on the headmaster, in a mixed school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ought' reads like 'should', but it is nought, the figure O; 'press head' is the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-educational schooling mixes boys and girls in one institution.

clue.text: Judge has right to enter row

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for right goes inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A judge has the right to join a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel, but it is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries a case, i.e. a judge or examiner.

clue.text: Way Santa Claus fills the stockings in due course?

definitions.text: Way Santa Claus fills the stockings

explanation.surface: Father Christmas stuffs the stockings at the proper time.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PRESENT-LY, the word reads as 'in the manner of presents', which is how Santa fills stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Soon, after a short while, is the standard sense; the other reads the word as 'by means of gifts'.

clue.text: Novel girl for ever giving warning

explanation.surface: A girl from a novel is forever issuing warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forever Amber' is a 1944 novel by Kathleen Winsor named after its heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Winsor's novel bears the name, and the yellow traffic light between green and red cautions drivers.

clue.text: Go to prison at start of tennis game

explanation.surface: Someone is jailed at the beginning of a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a stretch inside is one sense; in tennis, the moment to strike the opening shot is the other.

clue.text: Auditor's assistant plugged into 18

explanation.surface: An accountant's helper is plugged into something.
explanation.walkthrough: An auditor here is a listener, not an accountant; 18 is EARHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that amplifies sound helps a listener, and it is worn in the ear canal.

clue.text: Undisturbed right to enter professional payment

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for right goes inside the word for payment

parts.note: a fee is the payment charged by a professional such as a lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone has a quiet entitlement to collect a professional's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unoccupied or unhindered means one is at liberty.

clue.text: Project on behalf of champion

parts.note: to project is to jut out, to stick up
for means on behalf of

explanation.surface: A project is run on behalf of a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' is a verb, to protrude, not a scheme; 'champion' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion someone is to defend or support them.

clue.text: Nothing before end of May is wicked

indicators.note: before means the word for nothing comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: naught means nothing

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of May is used

explanation.surface: Doing nothing before the end of May is sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being badly behaved or mischievous is the sense here, given as an adjective after 'is'.

clue.text: Child joins family in small drink

parts.note: a nipper is a small child
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A child goes to join relations for a little drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipperkin is an old measure of liquor, about half a pint or less.

clue.text: Join the missing persons? Don't be such a pest

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and disappear and stop being annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming mislaid would put one among those who vanish, and 'go away' is the brusque dismissal of a nuisance.

clue.text: Job at Lancing?

parts.note: Lancing looks like the Sussex school or town, but lancing a boil is surgery, so a job at it is surgical work

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a post at Lancing, an English public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing is a town and public school in Sussex; read as lancing a boil it is surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical procedure such as lancing an abscess is the job meant.

clue.text: Venture to let piano continue

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
to resume is to continue after a pause

explanation.surface: Someone dares to let a pianist carry on playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume to do something is to dare or take the liberty of doing it.

clue.text: A role he switches to provide opening for listener

indicators.note: switches means the letters of these three words change places

explanation.surface: An actor swaps parts to give an audience member a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' reorders the letters of A ROLE HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hole in the head through which one hears is the slang meant.

clue.text: Target practice at Ambridge

parts.note: Ambridge is the village of the radio soap The Archers, so its practice sounds like the shooting of arrows

explanation.surface: Villagers in the fictional Ambridge practise shooting at targets.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the village in The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family named Archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting arrows at a target is the sport, and the Archer family's doings at Ambridge suggest the same word.

clue.text: A tree not without heart needs food

parts.note: a lime is a linden tree

indicators.note: without heart means the middle letter of not is removed

parts.note: the word not, before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A tree that is not heartless needs nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without heart' takes the O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is nourishment, sustenance for the body.

clue.text: Comfortable? The ayes might have it

indicators.note: the parliamentary 'the ayes have it' is twisted so that the letters of ayes may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: In a vote someone asks if all is well, since the yes votes may win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might have it' plays on the Speaker's call 'the ayes have it' and signals rearranging AYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed or at ease is the sense.

clue.text: Beast in the way always

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: An animal is forever blocking the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated bull, a bovine animal.

clue.text: Skill with which one copper departed coherent

parts.note: art means skill
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: A skilled policeman left speaking clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in clear, well-connected words is the sense.

clue.text: Spurred for example both ways by daughter

indicators.note: both ways means the abbreviation is written forwards and then backwards

explanation.surface: A daughter urged someone on, for instance in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' means the abbreviation for 'for example' is written forwards and then backwards, before the daughter's letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To be egged on is to be urged or goaded.

clue.text: Man maybe — but not according to Donne

definitions.text: Man maybe — but not according to Donne

parts.words: Man maybe — but not according to Donne
parts.note: the ... of Man is an example, while John Donne wrote that no man is an island

explanation.surface: A man might be one thing, yet the poet Donne said otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; Donne's 'No man is an island' denies the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a piece of land in the sea, and Donne's line denies any man is such land.

clue.text: Hangs on to heart of count

parts.note: keeps means hangs on to
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hold of the essence of a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman, but it is a verb, to tally.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tally of points in a game is to record the running total.

clue.text: Night out for cast

explanation.surface: An evening on the town for a theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild spell of enjoyment is one sense; to throw or hurl is the other.

clue.text: Look after railwayman going to south-east

parts.note: NUR is the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

explanation.surface: A railway worker heads to the south-east to care for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR, the British National Union of Railwaymen, stands in for a railwayman here.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone who is ill is to care for them.

clue.text: Drone then could be seated majestically

indicators.note: could be means the letters of these two words may form something else

explanation.surface: A drone might be given a royal seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch installed on the throne sits in state.
